Title: Cola-Braised Chicken Thighs

Items: 1 red pepper, deseeded and cut into chunks
1 yellow pepper, deseeded and cut into chunks
Tomato base: 3 tbsp tomato purée OR 5 tbsp ketchup (or a combo totalling ~5 tbsp)
Salt, to taste (adjust at the end)

Instructions: Marinate (20–60 min): Mix 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 2 tbsp cola, 2 minced garlic cloves, ~10 g minced/grated ginger, and a few grinds of black pepper. Add ~800 g chicken thighs, coat well, and refrigerate for 20–60 minutes.
Prep for searing: Remove chicken from the marinade and pat dry with kitchen roll. Reserve the marinade for later.
Brown the chicken: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Brown chicken well on both sides (about 3–5 minutes per side; skin-side down first if using skin-on). Remove to a plate.
Cook the veg: Reduce heat to medium. Add 1 finely chopped large onion and cook 6–10 minutes until softened. Add 1 red pepper (chunks) and 1 yellow pepper (chunks) and cook 2–3 minutes.

Build the sauce: Stir in 1 tsp dried oregano, 1/2 tsp mustard powder, and 1 tbsp light brown sugar. Add tomato base (3 tbsp tomato purée OR 5 tbsp ketchup, or a mix totalling ~5 tbsp) and cook 30 seconds. Pour in the reserved marinade, 330 ml cola, and 250–300 ml chicken stock. Bring to the boil, scraping up any browned bits.
Braise: Return chicken (and any juices) to the pan. Add 1 cinnamon stick (optional). Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes.

Reduce to sticky: Remove lid and simmer 15–30 minutes more, turning chicken occasionally, until sauce is glossy and reduced and chicken is cooked through (74°C / 165°F internal). Taste and add salt and pepper if needed.
Optional thicken: Mix 2 tbsp cornflour with 80 ml water. Remove chicken, bring sauce to a boil, whisk in a little slurry at a time until it coats a spoon, then return chicken to coat.
Finish + serve: Remove the cinnamon stick (if used). Top with 2 sliced spring onions and 1 tsp sesame seeds. Serve with rice (or pasta).
Customizations: For a less tangy sauce, lean more toward tomato purée; for a sweeter, stickier glaze, lean more toward ketchup.
Boneless/skinless thighs cook faster; start checking around the 20–25 minute mark after braising begins.
ServingSuggestions: Serve with rice (best for soaking up the sauce) or pasta.
Add steamed greens on the side (broccoli, green beans).
